body.statement:
Put \(q=Sd\) and suppose \(\delta_0<1/2\).  There are constants
\(c_0>0\) and \(\eta_0>0\), depending only on fixed class parameters, such
that for all sufficiently large \(N\) the base Holder model class
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) contains two laws whose realized interior
paths are separated by order \(N^{-1/2}\), whose observed-data total
variation distance is at most \(1-\eta_0\), and whose causal targets are
separated by at least \(c_0N^{-\kappa/2}\).  The training and treated-event
observed laws can be chosen identical; only the donor-location experiment
and transported untreated potential mean differ.  For every fixed
\(\epsilon_4>0\), the finite-support donor laws can be chosen with a common
exact covariance \(\Sigma\) satisfying the ellipticity bounds and with
standardized fourth moment at most \(q^2+\epsilon_4\).  This last property
belongs to the witness and is not a model assumption.  No lower
local-modulus condition is used.
body.justification: The donor pair isolates the root-\(N\) query displacement and rough-Holder modulus; its finite-support moment bound is verified locally for arbitrary positive slack.
body.gap: Strict interior slack is needed to move the query while retaining admissibility.
body.consumer: Generated-query MSE and expected-length converses use this channel.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(q=Sd\), fix \(\epsilon_4>0\), and take the interior reference query
\(z^{(0)}=\tfrac12\mathbf 1_q\).  Apply
\texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} with \(\Sigma=I_q\) and a fixed overlap level \(\eta_0\in(0,1)\).  The inequalities
\(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\) make this covariance admissible.  After reducing the lemma's displacement constant if necessary, for all sufficiently large \(N\) it supplies finite-support donor laws \(G_0,G_1\) with
\[
 \mathbb E_{G_v}Z=z^{(v)},
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}_{G_v}(Z)=I_q,
 \qquad \|G_1^{\otimes N}-G_0^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le1-\eta_0,                                               \tag{1}
\]
\[
 \|z^{(1)}-z^{(0)}\|_2=c_*N^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{G_v}\|Z-z^{(v)}\|_2^4\le q^2+\epsilon_4.      \tag{2}
\]
The displacement has a single signed coordinate, say coordinate \(k\) of cohort one, and both queries satisfy the \(\delta_0\)-interior restriction.  The last inequality is only a verified feature of these finite-support witnesses.

Use the same independent uniform exact design under both laws.  If
\(0<\lambda\le1\), define
\[
 m_1(x)=b_0+b_1|x_k-z^{(0)}_{1k}|^\lambda;                  \tag{3}
\]
if \(\lambda>1\), define instead
\[
 m_1(x)=b_0+b_1e_k^\top(x-z^{(0)}_1),                       \tag{4}
\]
with the sign of \(e_k\) chosen to agree with the donor displacement.  Set every other \(m_s\) equal to \(b_0\).  For (3), the inequality
\(|u^\lambda-v^\lambda|\le|u-v|^\lambda\) verifies the rough Holder condition.  The affine function (4) belongs to every higher-order Holder ball after choosing \(b_1\) small.  Choose positive \(b_0,b_1\) sufficiently small that all regression and potential wealth values lie strictly between zero and \(B\).  With \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\), (2)--(4) imply
\[
 |m_1(z_1^{(1)})-m_1(z_1^{(0)})|
 \ge cN^{-\kappa/2}.                                       \tag{5}
\]

Set the observed training responses deterministically to
\(Q_{sti}=m_s(X_{st})\), and use the same positive constant treated observation for every cohort and replica under both alternatives.  Put
\[
 B_{si}(1)=B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}},
 \qquad B_{si}(0)=m_s(z_s^{(v)})                             \tag{6}
\]
under alternative \(v\).  These potential levels satisfy
\texttt{def:buyhold-level}: take baseline wealth one, horizon-zero return equal to the desired positive wealth minus one, and every later return zero.  Consequently every return exceeds \(-1\).  Equations (3)--(6) verify boundedness, centering, consistency, and event-date transport.  The uniform design has density one and zero beta-mixing coefficients, histories may be taken independent, and the donors are independent of the panel.  Thus both laws belong to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).

The complete observed training and treated-event laws coincide under the alternatives, so the total variation distance of the full observations is the donor distance in (1).  Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} and (5) give
\[
 |\tau_1(z^{(1)})-\tau_0(z^{(0)})|
 =\pi_1|m_1(z_1^{(1)})-m_1(z_1^{(0)})|
 \ge c_0N^{-\kappa/2}.                                     \tag{7}
\]
This proves the root-\(N\) location separation, bounded testing distance, and rough-Holder target separation.  No deconvolution or class-wide donor fourth-moment premise is present.
